tob-4030: Miguel de Cervantes’s great novel trails a daydreaming gentleman who reads too many romances, straps on armor, and rides out as a knight — with the canny peasant Sancho Panza beside him. Half farce, half heartbreak, it is the first modern novel and maybe the greatest. Four hundred years on, the Don still charges his windmills.
tob-4230: William Gemmell’s Diamond Sutra gives the Buddha’s word that all we see is dreamlike and fleeting — no thing keeps a fixed self. Short enough for an hour’s read, deep enough for a lifetime’s pondering. The 868 printed copy at Dunhuang makes this the oldest dated printed book on earth.
tob-9047-60230: The second volume of Pliny’s Natural History marches on through living things — beasts, birds, fishes, and creeping things, with their ways and marvels. Pliny the tireless hoarder never met a fact too odd to set down. Bostock’s Victorian hand keeps the wonder whole.
tob-4130: The first of Mead’s Thrice-Greatest Hermes books musters his Hermes studies — the writ’s story, its thought, its seat in latter-day antiquity. His work bore Thrice-Great Hermes to English readers. The volumes are the classic English handling of the Hermetica.
cia-0000112330: A January 1990 report pairing an overview of Ukraine's Academy of Sciences with the Antonov aircraft design bureau — the truncated title cuts off the rest. As the Soviet Union cracked apart, its scientific crown jewels were up for grabs. The document shows the CIA inventorying Soviet brainpower on the eve of the breakup.
cia-0000112830: A September 1945 name list of Germans in Shanghai connected with intelligence and propaganda. As the war ended, the Allies inventoried every German operative in China — spies, press men, and agents of influence. The document is a census of a defeated network, name by name.
cia-0000118930: An August 1965 document on a September 15 statement about the Dominican Republic by J. William Fulbright — the archive truncates his name. cia-0000119730: A September 1956 report, its title garbled, on Hungarian university reforms emphasizing de-Sovietization. Students and professors were purging Russian models from education — the intellectual front of the revolution. The document shows a nation trying to think its way out of empire.
cia-0000126930: A March 1971 report from China's Xinhua news agency on foreign visitors arriving in Peking. In the year of ping-pong diplomacy, every visitor was a signal. The document shows the CIA reading China's guest list like tea leaves — who was welcome revealed where Beijing was heading.
cia-0000132430: A January 1960 report: Moscow initiating economic ties with Cuba. The superpower's embrace began with trade — sugar for oil, the deal that defined the alliance. The document marks the courtship's first contract: the revolution, bought and paid for.

un-ga-res-a-69-30: Resolution A/69/30, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The thirtieth act. The entry is the count: the number, the year.
un-ga-res-630: Resolution 630 of the General Assembly, adopted in 1962. The missile-crisis year's Assembly. The number and year survive; the judgment lives in the text.

cia-0000136730: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136730. The pre-invasion archive, firm-dated. The document is the archive: the before, documented.
plos-pone-0000030: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper: triose phosphate isomerase deficiency is caused by altered dimerization — the truncated title cuts off the rest. A rare enzyme disease traced to a misshapen protein pair. The paper is the cause: the pairing, altered.

the-united-states-of-america-part-1-1783: Historian Edwin Erle Sparks opens his survey of the young American republic with the critical years from independence to Jackson. The Constitution, westward expansion, and the birth of party politics are treated with scholarly care. A solid, readable account of how the new nation found its footing.
arxiv-2605-08930: Safety training often bolts guardrails onto a model from the outside; this paper tries to make safety part of how the model thinks. Yi Zhang, Yuxin Chen, Leheng Sheng, and colleagues internalize safety understanding in large reasoning models through verification — checking the reasoning itself, not just the output. The 2026 paper is AI-safety research on models that reason safely by design.
arxiv-2605-09130: Conjugation spaces are topological spaces with a symmetry mimicking complex conjugation; the quaternionic version is subtler. Surojit Ghosh, Ankit Kumar, and Lakshit Pande study their purity — a structural niceness property. The 2026 paper is algebraic topology on spaces with a twist.
arxiv-2605-09230: The geodesic flow on the modular surface — the most symmetric of hyperbolic surfaces — encodes deep number theory. Pierre Arnoux and Thomas A. Schmidt offer an elegant model of it. The 2026 paper is dynamical systems with a deep and beautiful arithmetic soul.
arxiv-2605-09430: Autoregressive image generators are gorgeous and painfully slow, generating pixel by pixel. Junkang Zhou, Yefei He, Feng Chen, and colleagues accelerate them after training with FlashAR — no retraining needed. The 2026 paper makes slow generators fast, post hoc, without touching the weights.
arxiv-2605-09630: Byte-level language models chew raw bytes — no tokenizer — but compute scales painfully with patch size. Lin Zheng, Vasilisa Bashlovkina, Timothy Dozat, and Dan Garrette decouple compute from patch size with scratchpad patching. The 2026 paper makes tokenizer-free models practical.
arxiv-2605-09930: Fair allocation under conflict constraints — dividing goods when the parties are in conflict — demands new mechanisms. Sarfaraz Equbal, Rohit Gurjar, and Ayumi Igarashi develop those mechanisms. The 2026 paper is fair division for adversarial settings. It divides fairly even amid conflict.
arxiv-2605-10030: Aliphatic components — the non-aromatic parts — influence the aromatic emission characteristics of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. Zhuang Zhang and Yong Zhang study the influence. The 2026 paper is astrochemistry on what makes cosmic soot glow. It explains the glow of cosmic soot.
arxiv-2605-10130: Thermal object detection with open vocabulary, via language-guided cross-modal distillation — Thermal-Det. Yasiru Ranasinghe, Elim Schenck, Florence Yellin, and colleagues build it. The 2026 paper is thermal vision with words. It detects heat signatures, guided by language.
plos-pone-0003430: Systems biologists modeled how cells reroute alarm signals in this 2008 paper. Toll-like receptors, the immune system's tripwires, feed into a web of junctions where signals can split, merge, or change direction. By simulating how signaling flux redistributes at these junctions, the team showed how one receptor can trigger very different outcomes depending on the network's state.
plos-pone-0003530: Chronobiologists added a gear to the mammalian clock in this 2008 paper. The body's circadian pacemaker runs on feedback loops of clock genes, and the team implicated the F-box protein FBXL21 in keeping that machinery on time. By controlling how clock proteins are tagged and cleared, FBXL21 helps set the speed of our daily rhythm.
plos-pone-0003630: Ecologist Jason Fridley put America's plant invasions in world context in this 2008 paper. Comparing eastern U.S. invasions against global floristic patterns, he traced where the invaders came from, Asian forests and European fields, and asked why. The biogeographic framing turns the who, where, and why of invasion into a testable global story.
plos-pone-0003730: In 2008, Cortese, Sahores, and Madsen mapped a cancer protein's commute. The urokinase receptor uPAR, abundant on malignant tumors, was found entering and recycling back to the cell surface without the usual clathrin or LRP-1 routes. The alternate traffic plan reveals how tumors keep this aggressive marker on display.
plos-pone-0003830: In 2008, Bem, Meyrand, and Branchereau found rhythm networks with many moods. Their model of oscillating cells linked by fast inhibition and electrical synapses settled into multiple stable patterns. The multi-stability shows one wiring diagram producing many behaviors, a useful trick for flexible nervous systems.
plos-pone-0003930: In 2008, Hromada, Antczak, and Valone watched shrikes choosing neighborhoods. The birds settled near other species, using heterospecific social cues to pick habitat. The team tested whether the settlers copied locals or just liked company. The results show animals reading other species' choices when picking home.
plos-pone-0004030: In 2008, Cherian, Forbes, and Cook untangled iron, infection, and anemia in children. Hepcidin, the hormone controlling iron balance, rose with inflammation and some infections. In iron-deficient kids, the team mapped how cytokines push hepcidin up. The careful work clarifies why infection worsens anemia in vulnerable children.
plos-pone-0004130: In 2009, Herrmann, Belloy, and Porcher timed immune answers in kids. Temporal dynamics of interferon gamma responses were tracked in children tested for tuberculosis. The T-cell signals shifted over the testing window. The timing data sharpens TB diagnosis in the young.
plos-pone-0004230: In 2009, Becker, Korn, and Sienerth found lung tumors needing a stem-cell gene. Polycomb protein Bmi1 proved essential for RAF-driven non-small cell lung cancer growth. Blocking Bmi1 stalled the tumors cold. The neat dependency marks a lung-cancer drug target worth chasing.
plos-pone-0004330: In 2009, a UK team found exercise armoring the stressed mind. Workouts improved thinking responses to stress through lasting gene-tag changes. The exercise rewired stress coping at the gene level itself. The neat finding backs daily exercise as strong mental medicine.
plos-pone-0356630: Rolling steel perfectly flat under enormous force is a fiendish control challenge. This paper developed a finite element analysis-based flatness control and bending force optimization strategy for high rolling force conditions. The strategy keeps steel sheets true even as forces try to warp them.
plos-pone-0348530: German doctors monitoring coronary heart disease and post-stroke patients follow established routines — but why those routines? This qualitative study explored physicians’ motivations, experiences, and perspectives on monitoring. Their candid views reveal what actually drives real-world follow-up care, beyond the guidelines.
plos-pone-0357030: COVID’s hyperinflammation may begin with sabotaged vitamin D signaling. This paper showed SARS-CoV-2 infection functionally impairs vitamin D receptor signaling, driving interleukin-6-dependent hyperinflammation in mononuclear phagocytes. The mechanism draws a direct line from the virus to the cytokine storm that kills.
plos-pone-0355730: Rest is surprisingly hard to measure — especially for people living with chronic fatigue. This paper developed and validated the rest experience scale for adults with chronically fatiguing conditions. The scale finally captures what rest actually feels like, giving researchers and clinicians a real metric.
plos-pone-0355830: Why do promising faculty leave academic medicine before reaching senior rank? This national cohort study identified the factors associated with faculty attrition before promotion. The findings warn institutions exactly where their talent pipelines leak — and what might plug them.
plos-pone-0354030: Underwater photographs come out murky, blue-shifted, and low-contrast. Phys-Mamba is a physics-informed selective state-space fusion network built for high-fidelity underwater image restoration. The network fuses physical models of light in water with modern deep learning to bring the deep sea into sharp focus.
plos-pone-0356730: The broth that Lactobacillus bacteria grow in — even with the bacteria removed — can kill drug-resistant pathogens. This paper demonstrated the antimicrobial potential of Lactobacillus supernatants against multidrug-resistant bugs. The cell-free approach sidesteps the risks of live probiotics while keeping the killing power.
plos-pone-0335830: Overweight older adults need strength training that also builds their confidence to keep going. This randomized controlled trial tested integrating self-efficacy strategies into multi-joint resistance exercise for this group. The combined approach targets both muscles and mindset — because exercise only works if people stick with it.
plos-pone-0354430: When disease strikes a pig farm, depopulating humanely and quickly is a grim necessity. This paper studied farmers’ impressions and perceived barriers around implementing water-based foam and nitrogen foam depopulation methods at the farm level. Understanding what farmers think — and what holds them back — is essential for animal welfare policy that works in real barns, not just on paper. The findings bridge the gap between veterinary science and farm reality.
plos-pone-0347730: Malaria mosquitoes of the Anopheles tessellatus complex in Indonesia harbor hidden genetic structure. This paper mapped their genetic variability and population structure using ITS2 nuclear and COI/COII mitochondrial markers. The population genetics inform vector control — because you can’t fight mosquitoes you don’t understand.
plos-pone-0355930: Isatis indigotica — a traditional medicinal plant — may calm liver inflammation through multiple targets at once. This network pharmacology and molecular simulation study mapped its multi-target gene regulatory mechanism against hepatic inflammation. The systems-level analysis modernizes an ancient remedy with molecular precision.
europmc-pmc2844030: Cancer patients often waste away from poor feeding, yet care lags. This 2010 French tally gauges how often poor feeding strikes in top cancer hubs, what ups the odds, and what it costs. The team bared a wide, weighty problem. Their sums pushed food care onto cancer wards' lists.
europmc-pmc2850930: Mitochondria, the cell's power plants, fuse together to stay healthy, and this 2010 fruit fly study links that fusing to a known Parkinson's pathway. The team shows mitofusin, a protein that aids fusing, is tagged by the PINK1/parkin pathway. The link ties power-plant upkeep to Parkinson's biology. The work filled a gap in why losing this pathway kills nerve cells.
europmc-pmc2859930: Stem cells from marrow were thought purely healing, but this 2010 paper splits them in two. The authors propose a new paradigm: mesenchymal stem cells polarize into a pro-inflammatory MSC1 or a calming MSC2 form. Their framing explains mixed trial results. The split urged matching the cell type to the disease.
europmc-pmc2875530: Sepsis kills fast, and early warning saves lives. This 2010 review surveys sepsis biomarkers, the blood signals that flag the crisis before organs fail. The authors weigh which markers truly earn their keep in the ER. Their review guides emergency rooms toward faster, surer calls.
europmc-pmc2954830: Keeping gut stem cells balanced extends fly life. This 2010 paper shows preserving proliferative homeostasis in Drosophila extends lifespan. The authors' work ties tissue upkeep to longevity. Their finding links stem cell balance to aging. The gut proves to be aging's front line.
europmc-pmc2956230: Patients sharing health data online can drive research. This 2010 paper studies sharing health data for better outcomes on PatientsLikeMe. The authors show the platform's power. Their work legitimized patient-led research. Thousands now trade notes on treatments there. Drug firms mine the site for real-world clues.
europmc-pmc3043330: Trial reporting got a firm standard. This 2010 CONSORT statement sets rules for reporting randomized trials clearly. The authors' checklist curbed sloppy papers. Their work lifted medical publishing. Journals now demand the checklist with submissions. Bad reporting hides bad science, they warn.
europmc-pmc3075230: Brain rhythms split by birthplace. This 2011 monkey study finds gamma and high-gamma waves spring from different cortical layers. The authors reveal the split. Their work lights up neural coding. The split clarifies decades of muddled signals. Brain-computer interfaces use the cleaner signal.
europmc-pmc6524730: Predicting what a chemical does to a cell means knowing every signaling pathway it might touch. BioPlanet, built by the NIH's NCATS, gathers thousands of human pathways into one browsable, interconnected platform. Toxicologists and drug developers can trace a compound's ripple effects across the whole signaling universe - spotting both therapeutic promise and hidden dangers.
europmc-pmc6561930: Muscles stay strong only if their mitochondria keep the right shape - and a protein called DRP1 sculpts them. In mice lacking proper DRP1-driven splitting, mitochondria mishandle calcium and muscles waste away. The study links mitochondrial shape to calcium balance and muscle mass, explaining part of age- and chemo-related muscle loss.
europmc-pmc6598430: Caffeic acid - the phenolic compound that gives coffee its bite - may fight liver cancer. This review covers the chemistry of caffeic acid and lab evidence of its anti-tumor activity against hepatocarcinoma cells: antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and growth-blocking effects. The findings nominate a common dietary compound for deeper cancer study.
europmc-pmc6612530: Heart disease starts in inflamed, oxidant-battered vessel walls. This review pins vascular inflammation and oxidative stress as major triggers of cardiovascular disease: how they damage arteries and why calming them helps. The evidence backs anti-inflammatory strategies as the next frontier beyond cholesterol.
europmc-pmc6718830: Rheumatoid arthritis begins quietly - and early molecular snapshots may predict its course. Profiling gene activity in early RA patients, this study drew molecular portraits that distinguish clinical subtypes and forecast treatment response. The portraits promise care matched to the patient's disease flavor.
europmc-pmc6756230: Tau tangles mark Alzheimer's and its cousins - but seeing them in living brains is hard. This review surveys tau PET imaging: the tracers, the pitfalls, and why imaging tauopathies remains a challenge. Better tracers would let doctors watch the tangles spread in real time.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-30: A 2007 Government Accountability Office report on fusion energy — the long-promised power of the stars — and specifically America's contribution to an international experimental reactor. GAO found the U.S. lacked firm cost estimates for its share and that the Energy Department's fusion research needed better coordination. The report questions whether the country was managing its bet on fusion science with enough discipline.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1130: This 2007 Government Accountability Office report on beginning farmers finds the Agriculture Department needed to take more steps to show its assistance programs actually worked. USDA spent heavily helping new farmers get started, but GAO found the evidence of effectiveness thin. The report asks a basic accountability question: are taxpayer dollars really launching the next generation of farmers?
gao-gaoreports-b-309530: Could the labor board spend its budget on magazine and data subscriptions? GAO's 2007 money-law ruling draws the line for the National Labor Relations Board's purse. Dry question, real stakes — the call is one more brick in the wall of rules telling agencies what their dollars may buy.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1030: Folding Marine commandos into the special-ops family was bumpy in 2007, GAO's report finds — the Corps' raiders needed real management moves to mesh with the joint force. The findings track the growing pains of building a unified shadow-warrior team from proud, separate tribes.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-830: The SEC's exam squad needed sharper tools in 2007 — GAO's report says planned fixes would not cure the inspection program's limits. The findings push the Wall Street watchdog to examine smarter, not just more. Trust in the markets, GAO argues, starts with examiners who look in the right places.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-430: Missile defense's next leaps needed better homework in 2007 — GAO's report says the big calls on boost and ascent phases wanted stronger backing data. The findings demand the evidence come first. The report's rule: billion-dollar shields deserve million-dollar studies behind them.
pmc-13470230: A 2026 health economics study comparing the costs of healing venous leg ulcers with muscle pump activation — a method that uses calf-muscle movement to push blood upward — against other approaches. Chronic leg ulcers are slow and expensive to treat, so evidence that a cheaper method heals well matters to clinics and insurers alike.
pmc-13456830: This 2026 psychology study surveyed adolescents about cyberbullying — both as victims and perpetrators — and linked involvement to emotion regulation, metacognitive beliefs, loneliness, and perceived social support. The pattern shows which teens are most vulnerable and which mental habits raise the risk. The findings point schools toward the coping skills that actually protect kids online.
pmc-13439330: A 2026 pilot study testing whether contactless vital-sign monitoring — cameras and sensors, no wires — is reliable for walk-in emergency department patients after triage. If touch-free monitoring works, it could ease crowding and reduce infection risk. The single-site prospective study reports how the technology held up.
pmc-13438130: This 2026 medical imaging paper introduces DREME-PET, a framework that jointly reconstructs dynamic PET scans and estimates motion over time. Time-resolved PET tracks how tracers move through the body, but patient motion blurs the picture. Solving both problems together sharpens the images.
pmc-13428830: This 2026 paper summarizes the 2024 update of ESPOGUIA, Spain's clinical practice guideline for managing axial spondyloarthritis — inflammatory spine arthritis. Guideline summaries distill hundreds of pages into what clinicians need. The update reflects the latest evidence on drugs and monitoring.
pmc-13472130: A 2026 computational chemistry paper assessing the stability of molecular glues — small molecules that stick two proteins together — using weighted ensemble simulations. Molecular glues are a hot drug modality, but predicting whether they hold is hard. The simulation approach offers a way to test stability in silico.
pmc-13386030: This 2026 review surveys extracellular vesicles in acute myeloid leukemia — the opportunities and obstacles for therapeutic advancement. Tumor-shed vesicles carry messages that shape the disease. The paper maps a young field's promise and pitfalls.
pmc-13459030: A 2026 environmental study measuring natural radionuclides and assessing radioactivity in soil samples from Gansu Province, China. Baseline radiation maps are essential for public health. The survey provides the regional data.
pmc-13453530: In this 2026 Swedish population cohort study, researchers examined menopausal hormone therapy and liver cancer risk. Hormones and liver cancer have a debated link. The population data give a careful answer.
pmc-13457930: A 2026 English cohort study on mental disorders, mortality after heart attack, and how the COVID-19 pandemic changed the picture. The pandemic disrupted cardiac care for vulnerable patients. The cohort data quantify the impact.
pmc-13452230: In this 2026 prospective observational trial, subjective and objective cervical spine mobility were measured after two-level anterior cervical discectomy and fusion. How the neck moves after fusion matters to patients. The trial quantifies it.
pmc-13422330: A 2026 ARDS study examining the intersection of biologic sex and predicted body weight. Ventilation dosing depends on both. The intersection matters for outcomes.
pmc-13522930: In this 2026 plant molecular biology paper, transient aberrant RNA and steady-state mRNA levels set thresholds for sense PTGS initiation and amplification. The gene silencing trigger was quantified. The thresholds are the mechanism.
pmc-13464430: This 2026 dermatology paper studied physiological characteristics of high-sebum scalp skin and shampoo cleansing impacts. The oily scalp's physiology was profiled. The impacts guide product design.
pmc-13458030: A 2026 prospective cohort study of dual targeted therapy for refractory psoriatic arthritis — real-world effectiveness and safety. The two-biologics strategy was tested. The cohort data inform rheumatology.
pmc-13501530: This 2026 paper examined the long-term impact of a teleprehabilitation program on modifiable risk factors and quality of life after cardiac surgery. The remote prehab's durability was tested. The impact is the evidence.
pmc-13433830: In this 2026 ovarian cancer paper, HDAC2-mediated SMAD7 stabilization activated Wnt/beta-catenin signaling to drive DNA damage repair and cisplatin resistance. The resistance pathway was mapped. The activation is the therapeutic target.
pmc-13332330: In this 2026 qualitative descriptive study, holding complex spaces through relational work in co-design facilitation was examined. The facilitators' relational labor was described. The study honors the invisible work.
pmc-13459530: A 2026 paper on size-resolved lipoprotein fatty acid content as a novel NMR-derived trait associating with genetic variants that control lipoprotein metabolism (the title is truncated). The lipid trait's genetics were mapped. The trait is the biomarker.
pmc-13499530: A 2026 PET study showing viloxazine occupied the 5-HT2C receptor in the macaque brain in vivo — a carbon-11 CIMBI-36 study. The ADHD drug's receptor occupancy was imaged. The occupancy is the pharmacology.
pmc-13515430: A 2026 chemical engineering paper on the promotion effect of steam on hydrogen and oxygen separation in an electrochemical membrane reactor — investigated under aromatization reaction temperatures (the title is truncated). The steam's separation boost was measured. The effect is the process advance.
pmc-13425630: A 2026 review on just transition toward clean energy access with focus on lead-based perovskite solar cell technology — lessons, experiences, and future perspectives. The toxic-material dilemma was examined. The review is the policy input.
pmc-13506530: A 2026 scoping review of digital and AI-assisted approaches across the preeclampsia care pathway. The pregnancy complication's digital tools were mapped. The review is the evidence map.
pmc-13467630: A 2026 review of recent advances in barrier property enhancement of biodegradable polymer films — strategies and challenges. The green packaging's barrier problem was surveyed. The review is the materials outlook.
arxiv-2606-16130: Some heavy atomic nuclei decay by spitting out alpha particles, and predicting how long that takes is a classic nuclear-physics problem. This paper refines those predictions: it starts from the liquid-drop model of the nucleus and applies physics-guided corrections to the leftover error. The authors show the corrected half-life estimates match measured data more closely.
